content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `DB-High-Conn-Queue` sev=2 -> paging on-call

pagerduty: Alert details: service=postgres-primary, symptom=connection_queue_length>500, action=page -> link: https://pd.example/INC12345

sam: acked. I'm oncall. seeing a big spike in pgbouncer client_count and postgres waiting connections.

sam: quick metrics: pgbouncer clients ~6200 (normal ~600), pg active connections 1800, wait queue 520, pg 99p read latency 1.1s, write latency 2.3s. Redis (kvcache) 99p latency 750ms, evictions up 12% last 5m. :grimacing:

irene: tagging customers now, looks like a batch job is hot-landing traffic to the write shard. pulling query logs.

leo: can we confirm if this is a client spike or internal backfill? checking ingress logs -> saw a burst of /api/bulk-update from a single service IP range 3m ago.

sam: ok mitigation plan: 1) throttle the offending service via our rate-limit rule 2) put DB into read-only for non-admin routes (quick fail-safe) 3) trim pgbouncer client_idle_timeout temporarily 4) scale read replicas if needed

marta: i'm oncall in 18m. if you need immediate hardware changes ping me. prepping handoff doc.

sam: executing steps now. throttling via envoy: `kubectl exec -it rate-limiter -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/rule -d '{"match":"src:10.3.5.0/24","rate":25}'`

sam: updated pgbouncer config via configmap -> set `max_client_conn` from 10000 -> 12000 and `reserve_pool_size` 100 -> 200, reloaded. watch: `kubectl rollout restart ds/pgbouncer`

leo: note: increasing max_client_conn buys headroom but doesn't solve blocking queries. I see a handful of long-running UPDATEs holding locks.

irene: identified query pattern: `UPDATE invoices SET status='processed' WHERE id IN (...)` coming from worker-batch v2. Looks like IN lists of 10k ids being shipped.

sam: immediate to-do: pause worker-batch v2, ask devs to switch to chunked updates, and add `WHERE id IN (..)` -> `LIMIT 500` loop.

sam: pausing job: `kubectl scale deployment worker-batch-v2 --replicas=0` -> done. observing metrics...

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation schedule: next escalation to sre-manager in 10m if not acknowledged.

sam: after pausing, pg wait queue down to 120, pgbouncer clients 4200, pg 99p write latency 650ms, redis latency down to 180ms. still above baseline but improving. :thumbsup:

irene: beginning customer impact assessment: - web write errors 504 for ~2% of requests in US-East last 12m - retries observed - some jobs failed and will be retried. Notified CS.

sre-manager: good call pausing the batch. Can we run a short smoke to validate data integrity before enabling workers?

sam: yes. running integrity check on a sample shard: `SELECT count(*) FROM invoices WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '1 hour'` -> results consistent with pre-incident delta.

marta: I'll be taking over in 15m. sam -- please add notes to the handoff: what we changed, commands used, and the exact replication lag at handoff.

sam: done. replication lag: 3s on avg, 5s max. snapshot of commands used attached in thread.

leo: recommendation for postmortem: add query-size guard in the worker code, add circuit-breaker on write-heavy endpoints, and add a pgbouncer pool golden config for spikes.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: auto-ack cleared (sam). next escalation suppressed.

marta: taking over. i'll monitor for the next 45m and coordinate with devs to roll out the chunked update patch. please assign follow-ups in the incident board. :white_check_mark:

sam: handing off to marta, leaving channel. great quick team response.

marta: summary for handoff -> root cause: bulk update job shipped huge IN-lists, holding locks and piling pgbouncer connections; mitigations: throttled source traffic, paused workers, increased pgbouncer headroom (temporary), scaled read replicas if needed, data checks done. impact: ~2% write errors for 12m. next actions: code fix, add guardrails + runbook update.

incident-bot: Thread closed for handoff. Please add retro notes to /incidents/board/INC12345
